articles.title: DUSU ELECTIONS WARNING TO CONGRESS-----19-09-2026
articles.description: Deepanshu Shokeen has won the Delhi University Students’ Union Vice-President post as an independent candidate after being denied an NSUI ticket. Securing 30,615 votes, he defeated ABVP’s Ishu Maurya by 13,705 votes. The son of a DTC bus conductor and an Anganwadi teacher, Shokeen campaigned barefoot, vowing not to wear shoes until justice was delivered to students affected by the Satya Niketan building collapse, which killed seven people, including five DU students. The DUSU 2026 results also saw ABVP candidates win the President, Secretary and Joint Secretary posts.

articles.title: History of DUSU: From a ₹150 grant proposal in 1947 to national spotlight
articles.description: As vote counting for the DUSU polls is underway on Saturday, the story of how the Delhi University Students' Union came into being offers a glimpse into the humble beginnings of one of the country's most prominent student bodies. DUSU traces its origins to August 6, 1947, just days before India's Independence, when the university's vice-chancellor informed the Executive Council that a representative body of students desired to establish a university students' union. The Council agreed in principle, noting that a committee would draft the necessary constitution and procedure, and proposed a small grant of Rs 150 for the union's preliminary expenses once it was formally constituted. That proposal, made just before midnight on August 15, 1947, marked the start of an institutional journey that would eventually turn DUSU into the representative body for students from most Delhi University colleges and faculties, and a key arena of campus politics that draws national attention. articles.title: 'Era Of Hunting F-35s & F-15s Begins': Iran's Stunning Declaration Against US Military | WATCH
articles.description: Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has claimed that U.S. warplanes are now being “hunted” and damaged, pointing to a Congressional Research Service assessment documenting American aircraft losses during Operation Epic Fury. The assessment lists losses and damage involving F-15E and F-35A fighters, A-10s, KC-135 tankers, helicopters and unmanned aircraft. The latest claims come after reports of Iranian strikes damaging multiple U.S. aircraft at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, including F-15s and an A-10. The figures include losses from enemy fire, friendly fire, accidents and other circumstances, highlighting the range of risks faced by U.S. forces during the conflict.
